label: sec:beta-decay-magic-shells-preamble
html:
The preceding section established the categorical β-decay mechanism via the \mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V} channel of the complex volume (The complex volume \mathfrak{V}). It showed how the n \to v (neutron-to-vortex) transition emerges from the Bring action on the substrate, why the categorical tower depth fixes the leading-order half-life, and what the tritium example reveals about the Q-value cross-check. We now examine this imaginary part across the nuclear magic numbers. Here the real part (\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}, binding) is maximal. The magic-shell structure of binding and the magic-shell structure of decay manifest two readings of the same complex-volume defect.

The following blocks trace these consequences. Trace-ratio observables relate single decays to the broader categorical structure. Diagrammatic double-magic LR-fusion explains why doubly-magic nuclei (Ca-40, Pb-208) exhibit distinctive decay-channel exclusions. The magic-numbers-from-q derivation connects the categorical magic-number conjecture (rem:periodic-table-demand) to direct β-decay evidence. We conclude with the Strutinsky-from-graded-trace bridge, preparing for the large-scale-observations section.
